<b>Signaler une violence policière</b> <: Report police violence Give your testimony to the Ligue des droits de l’Homme (French human rights league), which records violence during protests.
Un attroupement peut être dispersé par l: A gathering can be dispersed by force after two warnings (“sommations”) go unheeded. They are announced by loudspeaker or by a signal (red flare, sound signal).
Rester volontairement dans un attroupeme: Deliberately staying in a gathering after the warnings is an offence.
<b>Si tu les entends :</b> éloigne-toi p: If you hear them: move away down a clear street, without running towards the police.
Tu dois justifier ton identité <b>par to: You must prove your identity by any means: ID card, passport, driving licence, even a witness. Carrying ID isn’t compulsory, but it avoids being held.
Sans justificatif, tu peux être retenu·e: Without proof, you can be held for checks for 4 hours maximum, with the right to have someone close informed.
<b>Droit de te taire.</b> Tu donnes ton: Right to remain silent. You give your identity and can say nothing else.
<b>Demande un·e avocat·e tout de suite</: Ask for a lawyer straight away, from the start. If you don’t know one, a duty lawyer is free.
Droit de faire prévenir un proche et ton: Right to have someone close and your employer informed, to see a doctor, to have an interpreter.
Durée : 24 heures, prolongeable une fois: Length: 24 hours, which can be extended once by 24 hours for most offences.
<b>Ne signe rien</b> que tu n’as pas lu: Don’t sign anything you haven’t read and understood. You can refuse to sign a statement.
Refuser de donner le code de déverrouill: Refusing to give your unlock code can, in some cases, be prosecuted (French Court of Cassation, 2022).
<b>Avant de partir :</b> verrouille ton: Before you go: lock your phone with a code rather than fingerprint or face, and hide notification content on the lock screen.
Pense aussi à sauvegarder tes photos ail: Also back up your photos somewhere other than the phone: it can be seized or broken.
Filmer les forces de l’ordre en interven: Filming the police on duty is legal.
Diffuser des éléments permettant d’ident: Sharing material that identifies an officer with the aim of having them harmed is an offence.
Floute les visages avant de publier, ceu: Blur faces before posting, protesters’ faces too.
Dissimuler volontairement son visage dan: Deliberately hiding your face at a protest where there is, or may be, unrest is an offence. The law allows an exception for a legitimate reason (health, for example), which you must be able to explain.
En <b>comparution immédiate</b>, tu peux: At an immediate trial (“comparution immédiate”), you can ask for time to prepare your defence. Ask for it.
Blessé·e : fais établir un <b>certificat: Injured: get a medical certificate as soon as possible, keep photos and witness statements, contact your legal team.
